title: The artefact coordinates of the helper, the error-map source, the header format and the ordering with the edge are not specified for the implementation
source: Change Register v1 N009 row; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 20 and 49; Ownership Map v1 (idempotency_key owned by PLT); no technical specification exists for the platform library
description: No source fixes the values the implementation must be built on. (a) No slide and no specification names the package name, the registry or the version label of the helper artefact, or the build path of the error-map resource, while Architecture v5 slide 20 only states that every service comes from the template and the shared libraries. (b) No source fixes the header format of Idempotency-Key (length and allowed characters) or the expiry window of a stored response that the filter applies, although Architecture v5 slide 11 requires the header on every POST and a stored response. (c) No source fixes which side stamps the instance member when the gateway answers on the owner's behalf: the edge error envelope is published by RWB-PLT-N001-CON and the pass-through of the owner's code and detail by the same story, but the split of the instance is stated nowhere.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11 (REST: RFC 9457 problem details, Idempotency-Key on every POST, 2 s timeout, one hop), slide 20 (every service from the service template and shared libraries) and slide 49 (OpenTelemetry with W3C Trace Context); Ownership Map v1 idempotency_key row (owner PLT, library object created in every service schema); no technical specification exists for RWB-PLT-LIB and no slide of the deck names the package, the registry, the map path, the header format, the expiry window or the instance side.
owner_role: Platform library lead with the platform architect
proposed: Fix the package, the registry and the version label with the baseline release of RWB-PLT-NF02-APP, fix the map path at the library resource root, read the expiry window and the store timeout as chart configuration with the platform default recorded at the wave 0 review, and record that the owning service stamps instance while the edge passes the code and detail through; record all four before the template pin moves.

title: The published problem-detail schema, the error-map table source, the expiry window and the stored-response scope are not specified for the contract
source: Change Register v1 N009 row; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11 and 20; Ownership Map v1 (idempotency_key owned by PLT); RWB-PLT-TE006-CON DDL contract; no message catalogue file in the read set
description: The contract cannot copy three of the values it publishes. (a) No source publishes the problem-detail schema beyond the RFC 9457 member set and the media type, and no source names the table the error map is built from or the path of the file shipped with the library. (b) No source fixes the expiry window of a stored response, and no source fixes the exact scope tuple of the response: RWB-PLT-TE006-CON publishes the DDL of idempotency_key with its unique key on the scope and the key, and defines neither the scope contents nor the expiry. (c) The stored-response column set is the TE006 working read and not a field identifier from the data model, so the contract publishes it as the working read and cites the gap.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11 (RFC 9457 problem details; Idempotency-Key on every POST; a stored response per key) and slide 20 (template and shared libraries); Ownership Map v1 idempotency_key row (PLT, library object created in every service schema); RWB-PLT-TE006-CON section 12.7 (DDL template with the unique key on scope and key, no scope contents and no expiry window); the read set holds no message catalogue file and no published error-map schema.
owner_role: Platform library contract owner with the message-catalogue owner
proposed: Publish the schema from the RFC 9457 member set plus the code and traceId members, build the error map from the message catalogue as a data file at the library resource root, fix the scope as the service, the operation and the key, and take the expiry window as a chart value whose platform default is recorded at the wave 0 review.

title: Local decision-record library: artefact coordinates, no-case publish path, chain scope and incident routing
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 20, 28, 29 and 41; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 16; RWB-E1-027 sections 12, 13 and 14; R-PREC item 1
description: (a) The artefact coordinates of the platform decision-record library - the group, the artefact name and the publication channel it is released under - are defined by no source; Architecture v5 slide 20 names the library as a shared capability without coordinates and the legacy story published the interfaces inside the module. (b) The publish path when a record has no case (an access event) is not specified: slide 22 and Template and Rules R4 fix caseId as the record key for the case events, and the legacy AC5 keys the event on the event identifier, so the key of a record with no case is a working read. (c) The scope of the hash chain is not specified: slide 28 and the Drools design slide 16 say the record is linked to the one before in the service's own schema, but not whether the chain is one per schema or one per service instance, nor the hash algorithm. (d) The routing of the incident that a refused or failed write raises is not specified: the legacy story names the platform administrator queue of the job and service monitoring, and the target keeps that queue while the channel belongs to each service's own alerting.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 20 (every service writes its own decision records locally, own schema with outbox + inbox + decision_record); slide 28 (hash-linked to the previous record, 5-minute completeness, strict mode); slide 29 (one schema and one login per service); slide 41 P7 (central decision ledger); Temporal and Drools Design slide 16 (chain_seq, prev_hash, entry_hash, append-only, JOB-14 at 02:00); RWB-E1-027 sections 12 and 14 (DecisionLogEntryRef, MSG-P7-003, platform administrator queue)
proposed: Publish the coordinates from the platform library baseline, the entry-id key for a record with no case, one chain per service schema with the algorithm shared with P7, and the incident route through each service's own alerting; confirm in the verification loop

title: Local decision-record contract: record schema, table shape, shared-topic envelope and message catalogue
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 20, 22 and 28; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 16; Template and Rules v1 R4; RWB-E1-027 sections 11, 12 and 14
description: (a) No published specification defines the record contract: slide 16 names thirteen columns (chain_seq, inputsRef, ruleId, ruleVersion, recommendation, approverUserId, approvalLevel, finalCall, actions, outcome, decidedAt, prev_hash, entry_hash) and the legacy story adds the decision code, the case, the actor and the idempotency key, so the column types, the widths, the constraints and the entry-hash algorithm are a working read. (b) The local table shape is unpublished: Architecture v5 slide 20 names decision_record as a library object in every service schema but gives no DDL, and the Ownership Map holds decision_log_entry for P7 and no row for the local table. (c) The shared-topic envelope is fixed for the case events by slide 22 and R4 but not for this event: the exact payload schema beyond the named fields, the ce_subject format and the key of a record with no case have no published specification. (d) No published message catalogue gives the entry format of MSG-P7-009 and MSG-P7-003, which the legacy story carries as text only.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 20 (own schema: business tables + outbox + inbox + decision_record; DecisionRecorded to rwb.decision-record.v1); slide 22 (CloudEvents 1.0 binary mode, schema registry BACKWARD, key caseId); slide 28 (local record plus central ledger, 5-minute completeness); Temporal and Drools Design slide 16 (decision record columns, append-only, hash-chained); Template and Rules R4 (shared topic name, event naming); RWB-E1-027 sections 11, 12 and 14; Ownership Map row decision_log_entry owner P7
proposed: Publish the record schema, the DDL template and the envelope as the working read of this contract with major version 1, and freeze them when the consuming stories pass their contract tests; confirm the ledger side with P7 in the verification loop

title: Library artefact coordinates, the policy cache time to live, the authorise payload and the split of the masking read between P4's policy and P1's read are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-037 sections 4, 12 and 13 (published package recovery.access.matrix with the ScopeFilter, FieldMasker and isUnmasked signatures); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 10, 14, 20 and 35; Ownership Map v1 (no api row for POST /authorise, GET /me/permissions or /masking-policies)
section: 3 Preconditions; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 13 Solution plan
description: (a) No source names the library artefact coordinates: the package coordinate, the repository and the publication channel that the service template pins are absent, and slide 20 says only that every service comes from the service template and the shared libraries. (b) No source fixes the cache time to live of the cached permission and masking policy, or the parameter key that holds it; slide 20 requires a cache refresh on the two access events and names no interval. (c) No source fixes the request and answer payload of POST /authorise beyond the words role, scope and DoA on slide 14, nor the answer of /masking-policies. (d) No source fixes how the masking read is divided between the masking policy that P4 rwb-access owns and the masked values that P1 rwb-source-data exposes, so the point where the policy stops and the data read starts is open.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-037 section 12 publishes three signatures and no payload; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 10 (each service authorises the object itself using cached permission data from rwb-access, 2 s timeouts, breaker per downstream); slide 14 (POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA), GET /me/permissions, GET /doa-limits, /masking-policies); slide 20 (AccessPolicyChanged and DoaLimitChanged to cache refresh); Ownership Map v1 has no api row for the three access operations and no table row for a library cache.
owner_role: Platform library architect with the P4 rwb-access owner and the P1 rwb-source-data owner
proposed: Publish the artefact at a platform coordinate with major version 1, hold the cache time to live in a parameter read through the parameters client, publish the authorise and masking-policy payloads from the words slide 14 uses, and state that the policy decides clear or masked while the data owner supplies the masked or last-four value; record the three shapes at the contract freeze.

title: The contract shapes of the guard and masker, the /masking-policies path, the audit record shape and the failure mapping are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-037 sections 4, 5, 12 and 13 (the three published signatures and the X1 to X10 exception table); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 10, 11, 14 and 20; Ownership Map v1 (no api row for /masking-policies and no row for the access-log write)
section: 3 Preconditions; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.8 Contract fakes; 13 Solution plan
description: (a) No source fixes the contract shape of the three interfaces: the input and output types of the guard, the scope guard and the mask applier, and the attribute set of the personal-data annotation, are absent from every technical specification. (b) No source gives the method, the base or the answer of the masking-policy operation: slide 14 writes /masking-policies with no verb and no base, and the Ownership Map has no path row for it, so the base rule of Template and Rules section R4 has to be applied. (c) No source fixes the audit record shape beyond the requirement that it carries the case id, the field id and the masked flag and never the value. (d) No source maps a timeout, an unreachable access owner or a malformed answer to a status and a message, so the fail-closed rule of slide 10 has to be expressed as the 503 with no business data.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-037 section 12 (three signatures with no payload), section 5 X1 to X10 (statuses and messages of the monolith), section 8 BR11 (the access log record); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 10 (2 s timeout, breaker per downstream, deny by default); slide 11 (RFC 9457 problem details, one hop); slide 14 (/masking-policies named without a verb); slide 20 (the two access events); Ownership Map v1 api rows carry no entry for /masking-policies and no row for the access-log write.
owner_role: Platform library contract owner with the P4 rwb-access contract owner
proposed: Publish the three interfaces with their types and the annotation with its field-id attribute, reach the masking policy at GET /api/recovery/access/v1/masking-policies, fix the audit record as case id, field id and the flag clear or masked, and map every access-owner failure to 503 with no business data; record the four shapes at the contract freeze.

title: The client artefact coordinates, the owner of the cache time to live, the refresh event name and the exact build-check rule set are not specified
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 042 Central configuration service and parameter catalog v1.md (sections 3, 4, 5, 12 and 13); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 11, 14, 20, 22 and 29); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (sections R4 and R5.5, DP-06 and DP-09)
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria; 12.4 Events consumed; 13 Solution plan
description: (a) No source states the coordinates under which the parameters client is published as a library — the group, the artefact name, the version scheme and the publication channel — although all 19 services must bind one version and the platform library is not one of the 19 services. (b) Two cache intervals appear in the legacy story and no source says which one bounds the client cache: section 3 and the criteria use the catalog entry refdata.cache.ttl-seconds (default 300, 30 in SIT, DL11), while section 13 carries the property config.cache.ttl-seconds = 60 (assumed; DL11) described as the cache time to live and itself a catalog entry. (c) The refresh event has no name in the sources: legacy section 12 calls it ParameterVersionApproved, a new internal event with paramKeys, versionNo and validFrom, and names no topic, while §R4 requires rwb.<short>.<Event>.v1 on the owner's rwb.<short>.events.v1 and the Arch v5 event catalogue does not list the event at all. (d) The two build checks are described in prose only: the legacy story allows the literals 0, 1, -1 and test code, speaks of numeric and string business literals, names the catalog key whose default equals the literal and compares the keys read through ParameterService with the catalog file, but no source states how a string literal is classified, whether the check runs on every pull request or on main only, whether generated code and fixtures are excluded, or how a product-group default is treated.
evidence: RWB-E1-042 section 3 (catalog file config/parameter-catalog.csv; refdata.cache.ttl-seconds default 300; case.entry.dpd default 90), section 4 steps 2, 3 and 8 (ParameterKeys generated from the catalog file; both checks; refresh on ParameterVersionApproved and at the latest after the cache time to live), section 5 X1 to X3, section 12 (Published interface, ParameterVersionApproved with paramKeys, versionNo and validFrom), section 13 (Package recovery/casewf/config; ParameterKeysGenerator, RwbMagicNumberCheck and CatalogCompletenessCheck; config.cache.ttl-seconds = 60 assumed; DL11); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11 (contract published before code, contract tests in every build), slide 14 (rwb-case owns rwb_case and rwb.case.events.v1), slide 20 (every service from the service template and shared libraries), slide 22 (CloudEvents 1.0, event name rwb.<service>.<Event>.v1), slide 29 (one schema and one login per service, Flyway per service); Template and Rules section R4 (topic and event naming) and section R5.5 DP-06 and DP-09; Ownership Map api rows for GET /admin/parameters and the four reference-load paths (owner P3, ruling ASM-A6-api-4).
owner_role: Platform team (PLT) architect with rwb-case (P3) and the ACE DBA
proposed: Take the artefact coordinates from the platform library baseline at the version freeze and pin them in the service template; read the cache time to live from the catalog entry refdata.cache.ttl-seconds and keep config.cache.ttl-seconds out of the client; name the refresh event rwb.case.ParameterVersionApproved.v1 on rwb.case.events.v1 by §R4; and publish the two build-check rule sets as the contract of RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, with 0, 1, -1 and test code allowed and test code identified by path and by annotation.

title: The published catalog and value contract, the operation status codes as a library contract, the refresh event name and the start-up error surface are not specified
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 042 Central configuration service and parameter catalog v1.md (sections 11, 12, 13 and 14); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 11, 20 and 29); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (section R4)
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.4 Events consumed; 14 Validation and messages
description: (a) The legacy story publishes a Java interface and one response shape in prose; no source defines a published, versioned contract artefact for the client, its compatibility rule, or the full member set of the catalog and value data contract, and the field identifiers DF-REF-132 to DF-REF-158 are carried without a published schema that binds them. (b) The legacy story states 200, 201, 401, 403, 409, 422 and 503 in scattered rows and only for the operations as the monolith served them; no source states those codes as a library contract that a contract test asserts, nor which of them a client must treat as retryable. (c) The refresh event has no name, topic or payload schema in any source, and §R4 naming is applied by this run rather than by a source. (d) The start-up error surface is a health check that fails with MSG-P3-032 and names the key and the environment, but no source states the signal a client exposes to its caller — an exception type, a health state, a metric — or what a caller does with it when the value appears later.
evidence: RWB-E1-042 section 11 (DF-REF-132 to DF-REF-146 parameter_catalog, DF-REF-147 to DF-REF-158 parameter_value), section 12 (GET /admin/parameters response members, POST /admin/reference-loads 201 and 422 with MSG-GEN-002, MSG-P1-002 and MSG-GEN-001, approve 409 with MSG-P7-002, rollback 409 with MSG-P3-015, the published interface and ParameterVersionApproved with paramKeys, versionNo and validFrom), section 13 (ParameterStartupCheck, health indicator failing when a required value is missing), section 14 (the seven message rows and their texts); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11 (contracts published before code, RFC 9457 problem details, contract tests in every build), slide 20 (shared libraries in every service), slide 29 (one schema and one login per service); Template and Rules section R4 (topic and event naming) and section R7.2 (section 12 tables); Ownership Map api rows for the five operations (owner P3).
owner_role: Platform team (PLT) contract owner with rwb-case (P3)
proposed: Publish one versioned contract artefact at major version 1 that carries the interface, the four types, the generated key set, the catalog and value data contract with DF-REF-132 to DF-REF-158, the four consumed operations with owner P3 and their status codes and message ids, the cache and refresh rule, the start-up rule and the two build-check contracts, with a fake; freeze it when the consuming stories pass their drift tests.

title: The chart values, the seed ordering, the probe and the alert thresholds of the library are not specified
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 042 Central configuration service and parameter catalog v1.md (sections 3, 4, 5 and 13); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 20, 29 and 38); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (section R3)
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 13 Solution plan; 15 Screens and states
description: (a) No source names the chart values of the library — the environment name, the catalog file and the cache time to live — or says which of them is a value and which a reference, and no source states what a service does when the chart value and the catalog entry disagree. (b) No source states the order of the catalog seed against the rollout: the legacy story loads the catalog and its defaults in a Flyway migration of the same application that reads them, while in the target the rows are the owner's and the readers are 19 separate deployments, so the seed job, its hook weight and its failure behaviour are a default of this run. (c) No source states the readiness probe, its period, its failure threshold or the health check path it reads, although the legacy story requires that a service with a missing required value takes no traffic. (d) No source states the three alerts, their thresholds, their routes or their severity: the legacy story raises an exception path in prose and names no metric, no panel and no alert, and the platform observability baseline names no parameter metric.
evidence: RWB-E1-042 section 3 (catalog seed file in the repository; the ACE secret store holds secrets per environment), section 4 step 4 (Flyway loads the catalog rows and the default values at deployment) and step 8 (every instance refreshes at the latest after the cache time to live), section 5 X3 (the service does not start; the health check names the key; MSG-P3-032), section 13 (V042_2__parameter_seed.sql generated from the catalog file; ParameterStartupCheck as a health indicator; the cache time to live as a catalog entry; feature flag rwb.p3.configservice); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 20 (every service from the service template: /health and /metrics for the platform), slide 29 (Flyway per service in its own schema), slide 38 (wave 0 builds the template, the Helm chart and the golden pipeline once); Template and Rules section R3 (parameters and reference data to P3).
owner_role: Platform team (PLT) DevOps engineer with rwb-case (P3)
proposed: Fix the chart values RWB_ENV, RWB_PARAMETER_CATALOG and RWB_PARAMETER_TTL_KEY with a bootstrap time to live compared against the catalog entry at deployment; run one parameter-catalog-seed hook before the rollout that fails the release when a key has no entry, owner or default; probe the same check as the start-up check; and raise one page for a missing required value and two warnings for a stale cache and a failed refresh from the library's own metrics.

title: Reference-data client artefact coordinates, the cache time-to-live catalog entry, the refresh rule with no change event and the client-to-kit boundary are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-043 sections 3, 12, 13 and 14; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 20, 27, 29 and 44; Temporal and Drools design slide 15; Ownership Map v1 (reference_version, reference_row and lov_value owned by P3; rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case owned by P7)
section: 3 Preconditions; 8 Business rules; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.7 Tables owned; 13 Solution plan; 18 Traceability
description: No source fixes five values this library deliverable needs. (a) The artefact coordinates of the platform library — the group, the artefact name and the publication channel — are stated nowhere; the legacy module was a folder inside the one deployable. (b) The cache time to live is named as `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` = 300 (assumed; DL11) in the legacy configuration service, and no technical specification gives the catalog entry that now carries it in the rwb-case parameter catalog. (c) The refresh rule is fixed only by the absence of a change event: the legacy design publishes none for a version change, the target names no reference event for rwb-case on Architecture v5 slides 14 and 20, and Architecture v5 slide 20 lists only AccessPolicyChanged, DoaLimitChanged and RulePackageInForce as cache-refresh events, so how a consumer learns of a newly approved version is a read on expiry and nothing more. (d) The boundary between this client and the embedded rules kit is described in prose only: the kit fetches rule models from rwb-decision (DP-04) and the client reads reference data from rwb-case (DP-07), and no document states which of the two answers a caller that needs both, or how a rule package code is refused at the client. (e) The BRD section of REQ-CWC-016 is not in the legacy traceability table, which lists only REQ-DRI-011 and REQ-CWC-006 although section 8 BR7 cites the logging requirement.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-043 section 12 (published interfaces in recovery.casewf.refdata.api, no artefact coordinates), section 13 (`refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` = 300, assumed; DL11) and section 14 (message catalogue); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 20 (every service from the service template and shared libraries; the event list that refreshes a cache) and slide 29 (one schema and one login per service, boundary test in every build); Temporal and Drools design slide 15 (governance central in rwb-decision, services hold an evaluated copy); Ownership Map rulings on reference_version, reference_row, lov_value, rule_package and rule_package_version; no technical specification exists for the platform shared libraries.
owner_role: Platform team (PLT) architect with the rwb-case and rwb-decision owners
proposed: Take the artefact coordinates and the publication channel from the platform library baseline (RWB-PLT-TPL) and record them there, not in this story; publish the cache time to live as a named entry of the rwb-case parameter catalog with 300 as its documented default; keep the refresh on cache expiry and add no event, raising the contract to a new version if the rwb-case owner later publishes one through the inbox library; put the kit boundary in a contract test that refuses a rule package code and asserts that no rule row reaches the client; record the BRD section of REQ-CWC-016 when the Epic 1 BRD next version is produced.

title: The published reference-data client contract, the version and row data contract, the LOV-REF-TABLE code list and the no-version failure surface are not specified in a technical specification
source: Legacy RWB-E1-043 sections 7, 8 BR1, 9, 12 and 14; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 14 and 29; Temporal and Drools design slide 15; Ownership Map v1
section: 1 Story; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12.1 to 12.9 Contract; 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages
description: The legacy story publishes the two interfaces and the two records inside recovery.casewf.refdata.api and describes them in prose; no technical specification turns them into a published contract. Four values are therefore open. (a) The published client surface: the three method signatures, their parameter names and the exception type are legacy Java and not a frozen artefact with a version and a deprecation rule. (b) The version and row data contract: the legacy field identifiers DF-REF-159 to DF-REF-171 and DF-REF-181 to DF-REF-184 exist in the Logical Data Model, and no source states which of them the wire projection carries, in which order, or how a row is projected from row_data. (c) The LOV-REF-TABLE code list: the twelve codes are named in legacy section 8 BR1 and no source states that the list is the contract's code set, that a rule package code is absent from it, or that the holiday calendar has no code. (d) The no-version failure surface: MSG-P3-027 is fixed for the refusal, and no source states whether the client throws a checked exception, what the payload of the failure carries, or how a caller without Reference data R is answered.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-043 section 12 (the two interfaces and two records, and the sentence that rows throws NoVersionInForceException), section 8 BR1 (the twelve codes and the two exclusions), section 9 (VALIDATED, APPROVED, ROLLED_BACK) and section 14 (MSG-P3-027); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11 (OpenAPI 3.1, one hop, 2 s timeout, RFC 9457 problem details, contract tests in every build), slide 14 (rwb-case owns the reference data) and slide 29 (boundary test); Temporal and Drools design slide 15 (the rule registry stays central); Ownership Map rulings on reference_version, reference_row, lov_value and the rule tables; no technical specification exists for the platform shared libraries.
owner_role: Platform team (PLT) contract owner with the rwb-case owner
proposed: Publish the client surface as one versioned contract artefact at major version 1, carrying the legacy methods and records as they stand; publish the version and row projection from the legacy field identifiers with the three-value status vocabulary; fix the code set as the twelve LOV-REF-TABLE codes with the rule-package and holiday exclusions as testable sentences; publish the refusal as a checked exception carrying MSG-P3-027, the table code and the business date, non-retryable, with the caller's 403 surfaced by the access guard library.
